answer: A ceramic studio votes on kiln maintenance. A firing turns copper glaze on lotus tiles opal; a kiln controller signs each completed firing’s ID, poll ID and operator’s key. The studio checks the kiln log and issues a matching credential. Validators verify both signatures and key control, then atomically count each firing ID once across aliases and reissues. Extra votes require another firing and its fuel and labor, or another operator’s cooperation. A compromised controller can invent firings.
